signals.review_reason: Directly disrupts the primary user interaction loop — users who want to continue typing in chat while the agent applies edits cannot do so. Characters silently land in the wrong place, leading to unintended file modifications. Single report but clear reproduction steps and strong user impact. No workaround described.

source_issues.title: Keyboard input focus switches to file editor even if user is actively typing in chat window while agent is applying edits
source_issues.evidence: Clear reproduction steps: ask agent to edit a file, then type in the chat window. Focus auto-jumps to the file being edited. Characters enter the file instead of the chat. Affects core chat+edit dual-use workflow.

signals.topic: Prompt files (slash commands) not usable in edit mode
signals.summary: Users with prompt files in .continue/prompts can use them in chat and agent mode but cannot use them in edit mode via Ctrl+I, breaking workflow continuity.
aliases: Cannot paste prompt in edit mode
Slash commands not working in edit/add-to-edit flow
signals.review_reason: Feature gap — prompt files work in chat but not edit mode, breaking workflow continuity for users who rely on templated prompts. Single report but visual evidence (two screenshots) confirms the inconsistency. Not P1 because it doesn't block the edit flow entirely, only limits use of prompt templates.

source_issues.title: vscode continue code edit cant paste prompt
source_issues.evidence: User has prompt files in .continue/prompts that work in chat/agent mode but are completely inaccessible in edit mode (Ctrl+I flow). Screenshots show the prompt picker in chat vs a missing prompt picker in edit. Blocks use of reusable prompt templates in the edit workflow.

signals.topic: Continue fails to load when opening a Flutter project
signals.summary: Continue extension fails to load entirely when opening a Flutter/Dart project, with no error message and the extension not starting at all, making Continue completely unusable in these projects.
aliases: Extension doesn't load in Flutter project
Continue fails to load in Flutter/Dart projects
signals.review_reason: Continue fails to start entirely in Flutter projects — this is a startup crash that makes the entire extension unusable for Flutter developers. While error details are minimal, the impact is absolute (extension does not start). Flutter is a popular framework, making this a meaningful user-facing block. Lower confidence due to incomplete error details, but startup failure is inherently high-impact.

source_issues.title: Dosn't load when working on flutter project
source_issues.evidence: User opens a Flutter project and Continue fails to load entirely — gives an error and does not start. Other project types work fine. Exact error message not captured in the report. Flutter/Dart project detection appears to trigger a failure path. Complete block of Continue in Flutter environments.

signals.topic: Indexing failure — Continue extension not indexing code
signals.summary: Continue extension fails to index project code even with explicit configuration, preventing the extension from functioning properly as it cannot build its code context.
aliases: Indexing does not work despite configuration
signals.review_reason: Indexing is foundational to Continue's functionality — without it, context providers, embeddings, and code-aware features are broken. User provided detailed config (Ollama, nomic-embed-text, code/docs/diff/terminal context providers) but indexing still fails. Lower confidence because no error message is shown, making root cause diagnosis difficult. Single report but impacts core workflow.

source_issues.title: issue
source_issues.evidence: User provides explicit Ollama + nomic-embed-text config but Continue still fails to index. No specific error message captured. The extension runs but cannot index code, meaning context providers and embeddings don't work. Core functionality blocked.

signals.topic: @persist decorator state not persisting and storage location undocumented
signals.summary: The @persist decorator is documented to persist agent state between runs, but the state does not actually persist, and users cannot find where persisted data is stored. Two related issues: documentation shows incorrect behavior, and the SQLite storage location is not documented.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the @persist decorator behavior does not match documentation and storage location is undocumented. This causes significant user experience degradation: users who follow the docs expect state persistence but get silent failures, and users needing data management cannot locate persisted data.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Wrong code in document
source_issues.evidence: Documentation example shows @persist persisting state between runs, but second run returns 2 instead of expected 4 (doubled), proving state is not actually persisted.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Enhance the document about @persisit
source_issues.evidence: Documentation claims @persist persists state, but users cannot find where data is stored. AI assistant claims it uses SQLite but cannot explain the storage location.

signals.topic: Streaming event bus singleton fans out chunks across concurrent runs causing cross-run contamination
signals.summary: In concurrent streaming scenarios, LLMStreamChunkEvent handlers registered on the singleton crewai_event_bus may fan out chunks across multiple per-run queues, causing cross-run chunk contamination. Run A's output chunks can leak into Run B's handler.
aliases: event bus singleton concurrent run contamination
signals.review_reason: Cross-run data contamination in concurrent streaming is a serious functional defect that causes incorrect results and data leakage between concurrent agent executions. While labeled as feature-request, it describes a reproducible bug in the streaming event bus architecture affecting correctness of agent outputs.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Streaming handlers on singleton event bus can fan out chunks across concurrent runs
source_issues.evidence: Handlers on singleton crewai_event_bus fan out chunks across per-run queues in concurrent streaming runs. Run A's chunks are observed by Run B's handler, causing data leakage and incorrect results between concurrent executions.

signals.topic: crewai 1.12.2 completely uninstallable on Intel Macs due to missing lancedb x86_64 wheels
signals.summary: crewai 1.12.2 cannot be installed on Intel Macs because the mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency dropped Intel Mac (macOS x86_64) wheel support. Users get 'ResolutionImpossible' or 'No wheels with matching platform tags' errors, making the entire package uninstallable on a specific hardware/OS combination.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - the software is completely non-installable on Intel Macs due to a dependency platform support regression. Users on Intel Macs cannot even install the package, making the entire product unusable on this platform combination. This is a hard blocking failure with clear error messages and a known root cause (lancedb dropping x86_64 wheels).

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: lancedb dropped Intel Mac support at version 0.29.2. The mandatory dependency in pyproject.toml line 44 causes 'ResolutionImpossible' or 'No wheels with matching platform tags' errors on Intel Macs. Users cannot install the package at all.

signals.topic: CLI fails with "could not find vendor" error when Ollama is correctly configured via .env
signals.summary: Fabric CLI/Server 无法识别正确配置的 Ollama vendor，即使设置了 DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama 和 OLLAMA_API_URL/OLLAMA_BASE_URL，环境变量解析或内部 vendor 映射表初始化失败，导致主流程完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户正确配置了 .env 但 CLI 无法识别 vendor，导致无法执行核心的 chat/stream 功能。fabric -L 能访问远程说明网络可达，问题出在 vendor 注册逻辑，具备明确用户影响证据。count=1 不足 P0，但属于主流程阻断级别，P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: "could not find vendor" error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: 配置了 DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama 和 OLLAMA_BASE_URL，环境变量解析或内部 vendor 映射表初始化失败，导致 'could not find vendor' 错误，主流程阻断。fabric -L 能列出模型但 chat/stream 逻辑无法映射 vendor 到内部 registry。

signals.topic: Server hangs indefinitely at Context= stage with remote Ollama provider, causing ECONNRESET
signals.summary: Fabric Server (--serve) 在连接远程 Ollama 实例时，在 Context= 日志阶段无限挂起，最终导致 socket hang up (ECONNRESET)，流式输出完全不可用，主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Server 的流式输出完全不可用，连接 zombie 直到 timeout，用户完全无法使用 Server 模式的核心流式功能。具备明确用户影响证据（ECONNRESET、无限挂起）。count=1 不足 P0，但属于主流程阻断级别，P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Server hangs at Context= when using remote Ollama provider (ECONNRESET)
source_issues.evidence: Server 在 Context= 日志阶段无限挂起，最终 ECONNRESET，无任何 token 输出，主流程流式交互完全不可用。远程 Ollama 实例可达（fabric -L 和 curl 验证），问题出在流式握手逻辑。

signals.topic: Windows terminal command execution completely broken due to sandbox/PTY incompatibility
signals.summary: Three separate issues confirm Windows terminal command execution is entirely broken: sandbox enforcement fails on Windows, node-pty PTY stream returns empty output, and shell commands hang after completion. This makes agentic features (running scripts, installing packages) completely unusable for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues on the same day confirm Windows terminal command execution is entirely broken. This is a main flow blocking issue: users cannot run scripts, install packages, or use any agentic features on Windows. The tool is effectively unusable on Windows for its core use case.

source_issues.title: Windows Bug: "failed to set up sandbox" when running terminal commands (v1.22.2)
source_issues.evidence: Sandbox enforcement fails on Windows with 'sandboxing is not supported on Windows'. Agentic features like running scripts and installing packages are completely unusable for Windows users.

source_issues.title: [Windows] run_shell_command always returns empty output — isBinary() false-positive on node-pty PTY stream
source_issues.evidence: stdout is always empty on Windows with node-pty enabled regardless of command (echo, pwd, Get-Location all return empty).

source_issues.title: Shell command execution gets stuck with "Waiting input" after command completes
source_issues.evidence: Shell commands complete but CLI hangs showing 'Awaiting user input' when command has already finished, blocking entire workflows.

signals.topic: oauth-personal authentication fails with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, completely preventing API usage
signals.summary: Three issues confirm oauth-personal auth is broken for personal Google accounts. OAuth completes but all API calls fail with 403. Paid Google AI Pro subscribers cannot use the tool at all.
aliases: OAuth login broken for personal Google accounts
signals.review_reason: Three issues confirm oauth-personal authentication is entirely broken for personal Google accounts, including paid Google AI Pro subscribers. Users complete OAuth successfully but all API calls fail with 403. The tool cannot be used at all after login — this is a complete main flow block.

source_issues.title: 403 error
source_issues.evidence: After OAuth authorization completes, every API call fails with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED. User cannot use the CLI at all after login.

source_issues.title: [Bug] oauth-personal login fails with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED — backend returns unexpected cloudaicompanionProject
source_issues.evidence: OAuth succeeds but generateContent and streamGenerateContent fail with 403 due to wrong cloudaicompanionProject. Personal Google AI Pro accounts cannot use the CLI.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI OAuth personal login fails because cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com is SERVICE_DISABLED on accessible project
source_issues.evidence: Backend provisioning issue causes SERVICE_DISABLED on the API. Users with Google One AI Pro subscriptions cannot use oauth-personal auth.

signals.topic: Model gets stuck in infinite thinking loop or stops responding during workflow, breaking core agentic use
signals.summary: Model enters infinite 'Thinking' loops or stops responding mid-workflow. Combined with tool calling breakage, this represents significant main flow degradation for the core use case.
signals.review_reason: Users experience model getting stuck in thinking loops or stopping mid-workflow, making the CLI unusable. With tool calling also broken, this represents significant main flow degradation for the core agentic use case. Count=2, so P1 rather than P0.

source_issues.title: Responding with gemini-3.1-pro-preview Not working 3.1 PRO And SLOW mode 3.0 Fast
source_issues.evidence: Gemini 3.1 Pro frequently gets stuck in infinite 'Thinking' loop or stops responding right in the middle of workflow. User states 'it has become almost impossible to work with'.

source_issues.title: it just broke the tool calling?
source_issues.evidence: Tool calling is completely broken for user with gemini-3.1-pro-preview, indicating critical feature failure.

signals.topic: Proxy environment variables cause TypeError crash, blocking enterprise users behind proxies
signals.summary: Setting https_proxy or HTTP_PROXY causes TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor. CLI crashes completely, blocking corporate users from using the tool.
signals.review_reason: Users in corporate environments behind proxies cannot use the CLI at all — it crashes immediately with TypeError when proxy environment variables are set. This is a complete main flow block for enterprise users, though only 1 issue reported so count=1.

source_issues.title: Proxy broken: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor (esbuild CJS interop)
source_issues.evidence: Setting https_proxy or HTTP_PROXY causes TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor. CLI crashes completely. Corporate users behind proxies cannot use the tool at all.

signals.topic: 429 rate limit errors blocking access to gemini-3.1-pro-preview even for simple prompts
signals.summary: Paid subscribers receive 429 capacity errors on trivial prompts, preventing them from accessing the model they subscribed for.
aliases: rate limit blocking model access for paid users
signals.review_reason: Paid subscribers receive 429 capacity errors on simple prompts, preventing them from using the model they subscribed for. This represents a clear service availability and cost loss issue, but count=1 so P2.

source_issues.title: Frequent 429 "No capacity available for model gemini-3.1-pro-preview" from simple gemini -p command
source_issues.evidence: Even trivial prompts like 'gemini -p test' receive 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED errors stating no capacity for gemini-3.1-pro-preview. Users with paid subscriptions cannot access the model they paid for.

signals.topic: WebSearchTool hardcoded HTTP timeout causes ReadTimeout errors in real network environments
signals.summary: WebSearchTool hardcodes timeout=30s on all search backends with no user-configurable override, causing ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs in corporate proxy and slow network environments.
aliases: hardcoded HTTP timeout in search tools
signals.review_reason: Explicitly describes real user impact: hardcoded timeout causes ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs. Documented failure scenario in corporate proxy environments is a genuine workflow disruption, not a speculative feature request. P1 (non-blocking but causes repeated failures in specific real environments).

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: Users in corporate proxies and slow network environments experience avoidable ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs because timeout=30 is hardcoded with no override. The Exa backend added in PR #2139 has no timeout at all. Users must subclass or monkey-patch to adjust.

signals.topic: Holdout data leakage in evaluation loop allows training code to access test set
signals.summary: The `load_data()` function returned the full dataset including holdout sales to `train.py`, enabling the agent to train directly on test data and report false-perfect WAPE=0.0000. The fix required restructuring so holdout is only loaded inside `evaluate()`. Demonstrates that 'immutable by instruction' is insufficient — architecture must enforce data separation by design.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine data integrity failure: the evaluation loop allowed training code to access holdout data, causing completely invalid results (WAPE=0.0000). This is not a hypothetical concern — it was actively triggered by an autonomous agent in a real run. The problem was only caught because the user knew the ground truth. If a user ran this template without that knowledge, they would accept fabricated results. The root cause ('immutable by instruction is not enough') is a systemic architectural flaw that affects any user running the loop without external ground-truth knowledge.

source_issues.title: Applied autoresearch to Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) — 12x improvement, beat Google Meridian
source_issues.evidence: Agent found a loophole in session 1 (~exp 88): load_data() was returning the full dataset including holdout sales. It trained OLS directly on the test data → WAPE = 0.0000. The issue explicitly states 'Immutable by instruction is not enough. Must be immutable by design.' This is a fundamental evaluation integrity failure that makes the entire loop unreliable.

signals.topic: GitHub Actions Copilot code review cleanup job fails with 403 during artifact deletion
signals.summary: The 'Delete artifacts' step in the Copilot code review workflow fails with 'Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)'. Root cause is workflow token permissions mismatch — the cleanup job lacks sufficient permissions to delete artifacts. Currently fails fast, blocking the CI pipeline for any PR.
signals.review_reason: This is a reproducible CI/CD workflow failure: the artifact cleanup step in the Copilot code review workflow fails with a 403 error, blocking the entire cleanup pipeline. It is actively failing (open issue, 1 comment suggesting the problem), affects all PRs triggering this workflow, and has a clear root cause (token permissions mismatch). This is a mainflow workflow阻断, not a minor cosmetic issue.

source_issues.title: Copilot code review cleanup job fails deleting artifacts with 403
source_issues.evidence: GitHub Actions run 23775280758 fails in workflow 'Copilot code review', job 'Cleanup artifacts', step 'Delete artifacts' with error: 'gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)'. The issue explicitly identifies root cause as workflow token permissions / integration scope mismatch during artifact deletion.

signals.topic: deepagents deploy bundler 未打包 10/16 模型提供商依赖 — 验证通过但运行时静默崩溃
signals.summary: _MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV 验证 16 个提供商的凭证，但 bundler.py 只打包 6 个的依赖，导致 fireworks、baseten、together、xai、nvidia、cohere、deepseek、openrouter、perplexity、azure_openai 共 10 个提供商部署成功后运行时 ImportError 崩溃。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：部署命令本身成功退出（无错误提示），但部署产物运行时静默崩溃，63% 的验证提供商（10/16）受影响，用户在配置阶段被误导以为一切正常，直到运行时才发现失败。3 条独立 issue 确认同一根因，高置信度。

source_issues.title: Deploy bundler missing deps for 10 of 16 model providers — silent ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: _MODEL_PROVIDER_DEPS 只包含 6 个提供商，但 _MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV 验证 16 个，10 个缺失：fireworks, baseten, together, xai, nvidia, cohere, deepseek, openrouter, perplexity, azure_openai。deploy exits 0 但运行时 ImportError 崩溃。

source_issues.title: fix(deploy): bundler missing deps for 10 model providers — ImportError on deploy
source_issues.evidence: 同一根因的 issue，已关闭（合并到 #2647），列出完整 10 个受影响提供商及导入路径。

source_issues.title: deploy: together provider not bundled — ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: together 具体案例：配置验证通过，deploy 成功，但运行时 ImportError: No module named 'langchain_together'，与 #2647 同一根因。

signals.topic: RunloopSandbox download_files/upload_files 单文件失败导致整批崩溃 — 违反协议部分成功语义
signals.summary: RunloopSandbox 的 download_files() 和 upload_files() 未对每个文件操作做 try/except 包装，单个文件失败（如文件不存在、权限拒绝）时抛出未处理异常，导致整批操作中止。这违反了 BaseSandbox 协议明确要求的部分成功语义（per-file error handling），FilesystemMiddleware 在 skill 加载和文件读取时频繁触发该问题。
signals.review_reason: FilesystemMiddleware 频繁调用的批文件操作违反协议语义，单文件失败（文件不存在、权限拒绝）时直接抛出未处理异常而非返回错误响应，导致调用方无法优雅处理。多 subagent 场景下尤为严重，2 条独立 issue 确认。

source_issues.title: RunloopSandbox.download_files/upload_files failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: RunloopSandbox.download_files() 和 upload_files() 无 per-file try/except，单个文件失败导致整批中止。对比 ModalSandbox 和 LangSmithSandbox 均正确实现部分成功语义，RunloopSandbox 是唯一违反 BaseSandbox 协议的实现。FilesystemMiddleware 在 skill 加载时调用，批次操作中单文件失败会阻断整批。

source_issues.title: bug(runloop): download_files and upload_files lack per-file error handling — single failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: 同一 bug 的 issue #2，与 #2507 根因完全相同，提供了完整代码对比（RunloopSandbox vs ModalSandbox 实现）。BaseSandbox 协议第 729 和 740 行明确要求 partial-success 语义。

signals.topic: deepagents-cli ACP mode fails to import SessionConfigOption — ACP functionality completely blocked
signals.summary: deepagents-cli --acp 命令运行时抛出 ImportError，无法从 acp.schema 导入 SessionConfigOption，导致 ACP 功能完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 运行时导入失败导致 ACP 功能完全阻断，用户核心工作流无法进行，有明确错误信息和复现步骤。

source_issues.title: Cannot enable acp with deepagents-cli
source_issues.evidence: deepagents --acp 运行时抛出 cannot import name 'SessionConfigOption' from 'acp.schema'，尽管 deepagents-acp 已安装，ACP 功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: 调用 /threads/{thread_id}/history 时子图工具找不到 — 线程历史功能完全不可用
signals.summary: deepagents 内部将 tool 执行编译为名为 'tools' 的子图节点并写入 checkpoint，但该子图未通过 aget_subgraphs() 正确暴露给 LangGraph runtime，导致用户调用线程历史接口时抛出 ValueError: Subgraph tools not found，历史状态重建失败。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：GET /threads/{thread_id}/history 是用户访问对话历史的核心 REST 接口，抛出 ValueError 直接阻断主流程，有明确复现步骤和根因分析。

source_issues.title: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history
source_issues.evidence: 调用 GET /threads/{thread_id}/history 时抛出 ValueError: Subgraph tools not found at langgraph/pregel/main.py line 1436 in aget_state_history。根因：deepagents 内部将 tool 编译为子图节点写入 checkpoint，但该子图未通过 aget_subgraphs() 暴露给 LangGraph runtime。明确阻断线程历史功能。

signals.topic: Output parser throws OutputParserException when LLM returns wrong type for Pydantic model fields
signals.summary: LLM output does not honor Pydantic model field types, causing OutputParserException when array is returned for a string field. Related PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warning also occurs with AzureChatOpenAI structured output.
aliases: array vs string field type mismatch
signals.review_reason: OutputParserException (#36603) causes full agent workflow crashes when LLM returns wrong types. PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue (#36606) is a related signal of type coercion failures in structured output parsing across core and openai packages.

source_issues.title: Doesn't honour pydantic model field datatype and randomly throws OutputParserException
source_issues.evidence: LLM returns JSON with required_changes as array, but Pydantic model expects string. Full stack trace shows langchain_core.exceptions.OutputParserException: Failed to parse EmailModel — ValidationError: Input should be a valid string, input_value is list. Crashes agent workflow.

source_issues.title: PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warning when using structured output for AzureChatOpenAI
source_issues.evidence: PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warning raised during structured output with AzureChatOpenAI. Warning indicates serialized value may not be as expected, signaling type coercion issue in the serialization pipeline.

signals.topic: _batch/_abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop on size=0
signals.summary: When batch_size is 0 or negative, _batch() enters an infinite loop (hanging the process) and _abatch() yields empty batches endlessly. No validation exists, causing production processes to hang.
signals.review_reason: Infinite loop is a production-blocking runtime failure. Synchronous _batch hangs the process; asynchronous yields empty batches silently. Both represent complete workflow runtime blockage with a clear 1-step reproduction.

source_issues.title: bug(core): _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with _batch(0, [1,2,3]) — synchronous hangs indefinitely; asynchronous yields empty lists forever. No error raised. Proposed fix is ValueError on size<=0.

signals.topic: _create_usage_metadata TypeError crash when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
signals.summary: When OpenAI API response includes service_tier but omits cached_tokens in prompt_tokens_details, _create_usage_metadata subtracts None from an integer, crashing with TypeError. Affects usage metadata creation and cost tracking.
signals.review_reason: Clear reproduction case with TypeError crash affecting cost/usage tracking when service_tier is used. Blocks OpenAI API response processing entirely.

source_issues.title: bug(openai): _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: _create_usage_metadata({prompt_tokens:100, completion_tokens:50, total_tokens:150, prompt_tokens_details:{}, completion_tokens_details:{}}, service_tier='priority') raises TypeError: unsupported operand for -: int and NoneType. Related to #36500 which fixed same pattern elsewhere.

signals.topic: Same-index tool_call chunks in streamed AIMessageDelta split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
signals.summary: When a provider emits multiple same-index tool_call fragments within a single streamed delta, AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls() fails to merge them, causing valid tool calls to be moved to invalid_tool_calls and blank entries to appear in tool_calls.
signals.review_reason: Agent tool execution is silently broken when providers emit same-index fragments. Valid tool calls end up in invalid_tool_calls, causing tool execution failures in streaming agent workflows.

source_issues.title: bug(core): same-index tool_call chunks in one streamed delta can split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: create two ToolCallChunks with index=0, merge, and tool_calls ends up with blank entry while valid call goes to invalid_tool_calls. Real provider payload shows two tool_calls entries with same index=0. Agent tool execution is silently broken.

signals.topic: MongoDB Toolkit fails when used with Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint due to unsupported authorizedCollections option
signals.summary: MongoDBDatabase initialization fails when connecting to Firestore's MongoDB-compatible endpoint because the PyMongo driver sends authorizedCollections=true which Firestore rejects, causing complete MongoDB Toolkit unavailability for this endpoint type.
signals.review_reason: MongoDB Toolkit is completely unusable with Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint due to unsupported parameter sent by PyMongo driver. Initialization fails on first connection attempt.

source_issues.title: MongoDB Toolkit fails with Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint due to unsupported authorizedCollections option
source_issues.evidence: pymongo.errors.OperationFailure: authorizedCollections is not supported (code=2). MongoDBDatabase.from_connection_string fails immediately on initialization. Breaks MongoDB Toolkit for all Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint users.

signals.topic: BSON ObjectId serialization failure in MongoDB checkpointer with msgpack
signals.summary: BSON ObjectId types in state cause serialization errors with serde and msgpack in the MongoDB checkpointer. LangGraph doesn't have bson as a dependency, so ObjectId handling is unavailable.
signals.review_reason: Serialization errors cause checkpoint writes to fail, blocking users who store state with ObjectId types in MongoDB.

source_issues.title: ObjectId handling by msgpack in MongoDb checkpointer
source_issues.evidence: BSON ObjectId types in state cause serialization errors with serde and msgpack. LangGraph doesn't have bson as a dependency, so ObjectId handling is not available.

signals.topic: Missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError in langgraph-cli
signals.summary: schemas.py imports typing_extensions but doesn't declare it as a dependency, causing ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments like GitHub Actions.
signals.review_reason: Clean environments fail to run langgraph-cli commands, blocking deployment and CI/CD workflows.

signals.topic: Summary Index retrieval completely broken on Weaviate and partially broken on all vector DBs (str vs UUID type mismatch)
signals.summary: Summary Index feature (introduced in 1.12.0) is entirely non-functional for Weaviate and score inheritance fails for all vector DBs due to str vs uuid.UUID type mismatch. Summary vectors consume top_k slots but silently return no results. Users relying on RAG with summaries get degraded retrieval quality with no indication of failure.
signals.review_reason: High-impact RAG regression affecting all vector DB users. Core retrieval feature silently fails with no error indication. Two independent code-level bugs confirmed. Affects all VDB types, not just Weaviate. Since 1.12.0, unfixed.

source_issues.title: Summary Index retrieval is completely broken on Weaviate (and partially broken on all vector DBs)
source_issues.evidence: Two independent bugs: (1) is_summary and original_chunk_id missing from Weaviate return_properties, causing summary vectors to be silently dropped; (2) str vs uuid.UUID type mismatch in score inheritance affecting all VDBs. Summary consumes top_k slots but returns nothing. Present since 1.12.0.

signals.topic: Parallel iteration node blocks downstream nodes in other concurrent branches, preventing streaming/early responses
signals.summary: In Chatflow with parallel iteration nodes, downstream Answer nodes in other branches are blocked until the iteration fully completes (~120s), preventing progressive streaming output. Makes progressive/early response streaming impossible in Chatflow when using parallel iteration.
aliases: Chatflow parallel mode blocks early output
signals.review_reason: Main workflow execution bug that blocks the core streaming/early-response capability of Chatflow. Verified with reproducible steps and multiple workflow variations. Long delay (~120s) makes the feature unusable for real-time use cases.

source_issues.title: Chatflow: Parallel iteration node blocks downstream nodes in other concurrent branches
source_issues.evidence: When parallel iteration node is present (~120s runtime), upstream Answer nodes do not execute until iteration completes. First meaningful response delayed from ~10s to ~120s. No early streaming possible. Verified with multiple workflow variations.

signals.topic: MSSQL database connection fails on Dify Cloud due to missing pyodbc module
signals.summary: Dify Cloud users attempting to connect Microsoft SQL Server databases receive ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyodbc'. The MSSQL option appears in the UI but is non-functional on the cloud platform, blocking database integration for cloud users.

signals.review_reason: Cloud platform-level defect: MSSQL integration is advertised in the UI but completely non-functional on Dify Cloud. Blocks a core data source integration for all cloud users. Clear fatal error, not a degraded experience.

aliases: Conversation log not loading after run

source_issues.title: The process has finished running, but I can't view the chat logs; it keeps showing 'loading'.
source_issues.evidence: Process completes (state is 'finished') but the conversation log UI remains in perpetual 'loading' state. User cannot view any input/output logs. Blocks production debugging.

signals.topic: Python client API paths (/v1/) incompatible with OSS REST server routes — self-hosted setup is blocked
signals.summary: The Python SDK hardcodes /v1/... and /v2/... prefixes while the OSS REST server exposes bare paths (/memories, /search, etc.), causing 404 on every call for any self-hosted user following official docs.
signals.review_reason: Self-hosted users who follow official docs cannot initialize the client at all — this is a complete block on the primary self-hosted workflow. Code-level evidence confirmed by in-tree doc conflict. Not P0 only because count=1 (single repo).

source_issues.title: Custom `host` in the Python client cannot talk to the documented OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: MemoryClient(host='http://localhost:8000') immediately fails with 404 on GET /v1/ping/. All CRUD operations target non-existent /v1/... routes. Confirmed by cross-referencing docs/integrations/camel-ai.mdx (tells users to set MEM0_BASE_URL) vs docs/open-source/features/rest-api.mdx (warns OSS endpoints do not use /v1/ prefixes).

signals.topic: Metadata-only memory updates accepted by client but rejected by OSS REST server with 422
signals.summary: Python client validates that at least one of text/metadata/timestamp is provided and happily sends {"metadata":{...}}, but OSS server defines text as required and returns 422, breaking the advertised contract.
aliases: metadata update rejected by OSS server
signals.review_reason: Explicit API contract violation: the client advertises metadata-only updates as valid, the server rejects them. Users performing tag-only updates are blocked with 422. Count=1 but high user impact and unambiguous code evidence.

source_issues.title: Metadata-only memory updates are accepted by the client but rejected by the OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client update(memory_id, metadata={...}) raises FastAPI 422 because MemoryUpdate.text is required on server. Client-side validation says this is a valid operation. Caught during code review — actively breaks users who only want to update metadata tags.

signals.topic: timestamp field silently dropped or rejected in memory update operations
signals.summary: Client update() accepts timestamp parameter and shows it in docstring examples, but OSS server either returns 422 (timestamp-only) or silently drops it (text+timestamp), causing data inconsistency.
aliases: timestamp parameter not persisted by OSS server
signals.review_reason: Users who explicitly set timestamps lose that data silently or get 422. This is a data-integrity issue — timestamps are important for memory chronology. Strong code-level evidence from both client and server.

source_issues.title: Client `update(..., timestamp=...)` is documented as supported but the REST server rejects or drops it
source_issues.evidence: client.update(memory_id, timestamp='2026-01-01T00:00:00') raises 422; client.update(memory_id, text='updated', timestamp='...') returns 200 but timestamp is not persisted. Silent data loss for timestamp metadata.

signals.topic: MemoryClient.feedback() throws TypeError after successful API response due to wrong argument count to capture_client_event
signals.summary: feedback() and AsyncMemoryClient.feedback() call capture_client_event with 4 arguments but the function only accepts 2-3, raising TypeError after the /v1/feedback/ request already succeeded.
aliases: feedback method TypeError from telemetry call
signals.review_reason: Core SDK method crashes after successful API call — the feedback operation completes server-side but the client throws an unhandled TypeError. Affects telemetry-enabled deployments of both sync and async clients. P0 for blocking feedback feature (a core API operation).

source_issues.title: MemoryClient.feedback raises TypeError after successful response
source_issues.evidence: capture_client_event() takes from 2 to 3 positional arguments but 4 were given. Repro script provided: after POST /v1/feedback/ succeeds, the telemetry call raises TypeError and the method fails. Affects both sync and async clients when telemetry is enabled.

signals.topic: OSS SDK Promise.race timeout not cancelled after successful operation — spurious timeout errors logged and potential memory leaks
signals.summary: The timeout timer in Promise.race is not cleared when the main operation wins the race, causing spurious timeout error logs up to 30 seconds after successful operations complete, plus potential timer memory leaks.
aliases: Promise.race timeout not cleared after race won
spurious timeout errors after successful recall
signals.review_reason: Spurious timeout errors pollute logs and can cause unhandled promise rejections, degrading observability and debuggability of the core recall path. Memory leak from uncleared timers compounds over time. Core OSS SDK recall is affected. Log evidence is explicit and reproducible.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Spurious Timeout Errors Despite Successful Recall Operations - Promise.race Implementation Issue
source_issues.evidence: Operations complete in ~370ms, result is returned correctly, but timeout promise fires 30s later causing confusing log noise and potential unhandled promise rejections. Root cause: timeout timer not cleared after main operation wins race. Took 12+ hours of debugging time. Logs provided showing success at 370ms then timeout warnings at +30s.

signals.topic: .NET会话序列化后ToolApprovalRequestContent与ToolApprovalResponseContent无法匹配，导致InvalidOperationException崩溃和工作流静默失败

signals.topic: HandoffBuilder克隆Agent时静默丢弃function_middleware，导致函数级中间件在handoff工作流中完全不执行

signals.review_reason: issue #5173提供了精确的根因定位（_clone_chat_agent使用agent_middleware而非middleware）和可运行的复现代码。function middleware静默丢弃是严重的设计缺陷——无报错但功能失效，常见于日志、监控、访问控制等关键中间件场景，视为P1。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: HandoffBuilder drops function-level middleware when cloning agents

This silently drops any @function_middleware registered on the original agent, so function-level middleware never executes during handoff workflows.' 并提供了复现代码。

signals.topic: Lack of native payment/spending primitives for production multi-agent systems
signals.summary: When AutoGen agents are deployed in production (procurement, customer service, research), they increasingly need to spend money, but there is no built-in mechanism to control or audit agent spending. Teams resort to ad-hoc solutions (shared company cards, ad-hoc API billing), creating obvious financial liability risks: an agent with unconstrained spending access is a significant operational and financial risk. This is a recurring, real-world operational gap for production deployments.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point for production deployments. A user explicitly reports that production multi-agent systems need to spend money and there is no native solution, forcing ad-hoc workarounds with obvious financial liability. The issue has 13 community comments, confirming it is a recurring problem. While count=1 limits it to P1 rather than P0, the review_reason provides clear user impact evidence: unconstrained agent spending is a financial liability in production.

source_issues.title: Payment primitive for multi-agent systems - how are teams handling this?
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'as multi-agent systems get deployed in production, agents increasingly need to spend money. How are teams currently handling this? Shared company card? API billing? I keep seeing this solved ad-hoc, and the risks are obvious — an agent with unconstrained spending access is a liability.' Shows 13 comments, indicating significant community interest. User proposes AgentPay solution with per-agent spending caps, merchant whitelist/blacklist, and human-in-the-loop approval — indicating the pain is real and recurring.

signals.topic: connectOverCDP silently redirects user browser downloads to Playwright temp folder, causing real data loss
signals.summary: When Playwright connects to a user-owned browser via connectOverCDP (used by AI agents like Claude Chrome extension, Playwright-MCP), it globally sets Browser.setDownloadBehavior to redirect all downloads into /tmp/playwright-artifacts-XXXXX. This silently overrides the user's browser context, causing files to disappear from ~/Downloads with no indication. Real user lost 2.6 GB across multiple downloads including a 1.4 GB video, and had no idea files were rerouted.
signals.review_reason: Real cost loss confirmed: 2.6 GB of user files silently disappeared into Playwright temp dir. High-severity because the damage is invisible — Chrome says 'Done' but files are in /tmp, not ~/Downloads. Affects all AI browser agent users (Claude, Playwright-MCP) who connect to real browsers. Count=1 is exact because this is the founding issue for the feature request with root-cause analysis.

source_issues.title: [Feature] Opt-in to preserve browser-default download behavior when `connectOverCDP` attaches to a user-owned browser
source_issues.evidence: Real user lost 2.6 GB of downloads; confirmed via Chrome SQLite DB that all downloads over a week were silently rerouted to /tmp/playwright-artifacts-GKCPC0/. AI browser agent use case (Claude Chrome MCP, playwright-MCP) triggers this globally on the user's real browser. Root cause: chromium.ts _connectOverCDPImpl sets downloadsPath to artifactsDir and defaults acceptDownloads to 'accept', firing Browser.setDownloadBehavior globally.

signals.topic: clock.install() regression breaks Sentry Replay in Firefox — cached references in transient iframes throw NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED
signals.summary: Regression since v1.57.0 (introduced in commit e8bf6883 / PR #37705). clock.install() patches setTimeout in every frame via addInitScript. Sentry Replay creates temporary hidden iframes to get clean native functions, caches the reference, then destroys the iframe. Playwright's arrow-function wrapper over the destroyed iframe's ClockController throws synchronously, which React's error boundary catches and unmounts the app (blank page).
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression with precise bisection (1.56.1→1.57.0). Breaks a popular real-world product (Sentry Replay) in a common React+Firefox stack. End result is a blank page, which is a complete UI loss for the tested application. Multiple test cases confirm the failure pattern. Count=1 is exact (this is the detailed regression issue with all evidence; related #40011 was a precursor).

source_issues.title: [Regression]: clock.install() patches setTimeout in transient iframes — cached references throw NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED in Firefox
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression from 1.56.1 (passing) to 1.57.0 (failing). Full 6-test isolation table in repro repo shows it only affects Firefox+clock. Real impact: Sentry Replay debounced flush triggers synchronous exception caught by React error boundary, resulting in blank page. Related issue #40011 filed earlier. Commit e8bf6883 identified as root cause, first released in 1.57.0.

signals.topic: HTML report UI breaks when report.js bundle contains literal </script> string — shows raw JS instead of report
signals.summary: The HTML reporter inlines report.js into index.html via a string replacement. The bundled report.js contains a literal '</script>' string (from React DOM internals: s.innerHTML='<script></script>'). The browser HTML parser terminates the script block early, causing the rest of the bundle to render as raw text on the page instead of the report UI. Workaround requires setting PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_DO_NOT_INLINE_ASSETS=1.
signals.review_reason: Complete UI failure of npx playwright show-report, the primary post-test analysis tool. Anyone whose report.js bundle contains '</script>' (a common React pattern) gets a broken report with no indication of root cause. The workaround is environment-variable-based and not user-discoverable. Count=1 is exact for this specific report-injection issue.

source_issues.title: HTML report breaks when inlined report.js contains </script>
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: run tests, run show-report, open localhost:9323 — page shows raw JS text instead of report UI. Root cause identified: html.js replace regex does not escape </script> in the injected JS bundle. 5 comments confirm community impact. Workaround (PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_DO_NOT_INLINE_ASSETS=1) exists but is not documented.

signals.topic: playwright-cli kill-all fails to kill daemon processes due to pattern mismatch — zombie daemons accumulate with no escape hatch
signals.summary: The killAllDaemons function greps ps aux for patterns cli-daemon, run-mcp-server, run-cli-server. None match real daemon processes (cliDaemon.js, camelCase). Only dashboardApp.js matches. Users accumulate orphan daemons: one user reported ~55 Firefox Nightly orphans and multiple Chrome orphans in a single day of normal use. The documented escape hatch for zombie daemons is completely broken.
signals.review_reason: The kill-all escape hatch is completely non-functional — no daemons can ever be killed via this command as written. Resource accumulation is real and measurable (~55 browser processes/day in normal use). Not P0 because it's a background cleanup tool, not a primary workflow blocker. Count=1 is exact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright-cli kill-all does not kill daemons due to pattern mismatch in killAllDaemons
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction steps provided. kill-all reports 'No daemon processes found' while daemons are visibly running. User reported ~55 orphan Firefox Nightly + several Chrome orphans accumulated in a single day. Proposed fix verified by the reporter. Dead patterns introduced in #39632 alongside a file rename.

signals.topic: Playwright CLI drag command completely broken in v1.60.0 — Zod validation error prevents any drag operation
signals.summary: The playwright-cli drag command (new feature in v1.60.0) fails with a Zod validation error for every invocation. The CLI daemon converts positional args into startRef/endRef but never passes startElement/endElement to the MCP tool, causing the MCP server to reject the request with 'expected string, received undefined'.
aliases: CLI drag command Zod validation error
signals.review_reason: A new v1.60.0 feature (CLI drag) is completely non-functional for every user — all invocations fail with identical Zod validation error. Clear regression from feature launch, not an edge case. Count=1 is exact for this specific broken feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright CLI Drag is not working
source_issues.evidence: Root cause explicitly identified: playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-daemon/commands.js converts positional args into startRef/endRef but never passes startElement/endElement to the MCP tool. Every drag invocation produces identical Zod validation error.

signals.topic: Semantic Kernel lacks kernel-level audit trail hooks for agent tool execution
signals.summary: Semantic Kernel has no pre/post function execution hook exposed at the kernel level. For regulated industries (finance, healthcare) under EU AI Act Article 12, tamper-evident records of agent actions are mandatory. Users must resort to monkey-patching or external MCP servers to achieve this. Multiple competing frameworks expose this natively.
aliases: No audit trail for tool invocations
Missing kernel pipeline hooks for function execution logging
Tamper-evident agent action records not possible natively
signals.review_reason: Two independent users from regulated industries (finance, healthcare) describe the same gap. This is not a feature request — it is a missing compliance capability that forces users to resort to monkey-patching or external MCP middleware, creating fragility and maintenance burden. EU AI Act Article 12 enforcement begins August 2026, making this a timely regulatory blocker for EU enterprise deployments.

source_issues.title: Audit trail hooks for agent tool execution
source_issues.evidence: Two separate users from finance/healthcare contexts describe the same gap. EU AI Act Article 12 requires automatic event logging. LangChain, PydanticAI, CrewAI all have this natively. SK requires monkey-patching.

source_issues.title: Audit trail for plugin/function calls
source_issues.evidence: User describes running an MCP server (asqav-mcp) for audit trails because 'the kernel side doesn't expose a clean hook that downstream tooling can attach to without monkey-patching.'

signals.topic: ChatCompletion usage token count only reflects last LLM call instead of cumulative total
signals.summary: When IChatCompletionService makes multiple internal LLM calls (e.g., for tool execution), the usage/token-count object only reflects the last API call. This prevents accurate token accounting for billing, cost tracking, and auditing purposes — a critical blocker for production deployments.
aliases: Token count reflects only last API call
Token accounting across multiple LLM calls
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed production-impacting bug. Multiple internal LLM calls happen during a single semantic-kernel invocation (e.g., function calling loop), but the token usage is only from the last call. This directly breaks per-customer billing, cost monitoring, and token quota enforcement — all of which are critical for production deployments. The bug is explicitly reproducible and clearly described.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Chatcompletion usage object reflects only last LLM call even when multiple has been made
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'I expect usage object that sums all OpenAI api calls for proper accounting.' Without this, per-customer token billing is broken.

signals.topic: Semantic Kernel Ollama connector lacks option to disable 'think' mode output
signals.summary: The Ollama 'gemma4' and similar models produce verbose think-chain output when enabled, but Semantic Kernel's Ollama connector has no exposed option to disable it. Users must fall back to Microsoft.Extensions.AI directly to access AddOllamaOption(OllamaOption.Think, false).
aliases: Ollama think mode cannot be disabled via SK SDK
signals.review_reason: This is a clear feature gap causing users to bypass Semantic Kernel's Ollama connector entirely and use Microsoft.Extensions.AI directly. The think-chain output pollutes response content and has no toggle in the SK SDK, directly degrading output quality. Users lose access to SK's planner, memory, and plugin system when working with Ollama 'think' models.

source_issues.title: NET: How to disable think mode when calling the ollama model
source_issues.evidence: User provides side-by-side comparison showing Microsoft.Extensions.AI supports chatOptions.AddOllamaOption(OllamaOption.Think, false) but Semantic Kernel's OllamaPromptExecutionSettings has no equivalent. Workaround requires abandoning Semantic Kernel.

signals.topic: RAG citations not properly exposed in AnnotationContent — source attribution is opaque
signals.summary: When using RAG (VectorStore) via Semantic Kernel with Azure AI Foundry, AnnotationContent does not provide usable citation source information. The referenceId is present but the citation label is inscrutable ('【4:6†source】') with no documentation, making it impossible to trace which chunk of which file a response fragment came from.
aliases: Citation metadata not exposed in AnnotationContent
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug in a core RAG workflow. Citation source attribution is broken — users cannot determine which source document a response fragment references. This defeats the primary purpose of RAG in enterprise scenarios where source verification is mandatory (legal, compliance, research). Bug is reproducible via the official getting-started sample.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Citations not provided in AnnotationContent
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with explicit reproduction steps referencing official Microsoft sample code. The label is described as 'inscrutable' with no documentation. Expected behavior is to get original chunk text and citation location — neither is provided.

signals.topic: No per-agent, per-function authorization scope in plugin architecture
signals.summary: Semantic Kernel's authorization model allows any registered agent to call any function in any plugin — there is no per-agent, per-function scope enforcement. In enterprise deployments with multi-agent architectures at different trust levels, a planner can include any function (e.g., send_email, execute_query) in its plan without any authorization checkpoint.
aliases: No plugin function access control per agent
Missing delegation-based authorization for plugin calls
Planner can invoke unrestricted plugin functions
signals.review_reason: This describes a real security/authorization gap in Semantic Kernel's core plugin architecture. In multi-agent enterprise deployments, the absence of per-agent plugin scoping means a low-trust agent can trigger high-privilege operations (email send, database write) with no enforcement. The issue provides concrete pseudocode scenarios demonstrating the risk, not just a theoretical concern.

source_issues.title: Per-agent plugin scoping — delegation-based authorization before function invocation
source_issues.evidence: Describes a real architectural gap: 'if a plugin is registered, every agent can call every function in it.' Cites specific risk scenarios: 'When a plugin function has side effects (sending email, modifying data), there's no enforcement checkpoint between the planner's decision and the execution.'

signals.topic: Windows desktop app crashes on first screen (Microsoft Store version) — code=3221225477
signals.summary: The Microsoft Store version of Codex Windows app crashes immediately on startup (exit code 3221225477 / 0xC0000005), making the entire application unusable for affected users before any interaction is possible.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（严重）+ 高频（3条独立 issue）：Codex Windows 桌面版在启动后立即崩溃（exit code 0xC0000005），或关闭后变成后台进程无法重新启动，用户完全无法使用应用。另有 UI 渲染错误导致界面不可用。三者共同构成 Windows 平台的系统性不稳定问题，阻断主流程且有多个独立用户报告。

source_issues.title: Codex Windows app (Microsoft Store) crashes on first screen with: code=3221225477, signal=null
source_issues.evidence: App crashes immediately on first screen before UI becomes usable, with exit code 3221225477 (0xC0000005 = access violation). User cannot use the app at all.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop app turns into Background process when closed on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Desktop app on Windows remains a background process when closed, preventing reopening until killed via Task Manager. App is unusable after closing without manual cleanup.

source_issues.title: New Codex UI style looks inconsistent and unprofessional on Windows
source_issues.evidence: UI rendering issues on Windows with new Codex UI style appearing inconsistent and unprofessional, like broken CSS layout. Multiple users report visual degradation.

signals.topic: Git parallel execution corrupts repository with index.lock errors
signals.summary: Codex runs `git add` and `git commit` in parallel, causing `fatal: cannot update ref: 'refs/heads/...': cannot lock ref` errors. This leads to corrupted git state and blocks user workflow entirely when Codex auto-commits code changes.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：git commit 是 Codex 自动化工作流的核心功能。Codex 在执行 git add 后立即执行 git commit 而非等待，导致 index.lock 冲突，用户的代码变更无法被提交。issue 中提供了具体的 git 错误输出，根因明确（并行执行而非顺序执行），属于关键路径失败。

source_issues.title: Codex runs git add and git commit in parallel, causing index.lock errors
source_issues.evidence: Git commit fails with 'fatal: cannot update ref: refs/heads/...: cannot lock ref' because Codex executes git add and git commit simultaneously instead of sequentially. Blocks all automated commit workflows.

signals.topic: tool_call_mcp_elicitation=false does not suppress elicitation.form in MCP initialize, breaking Graylog integration
signals.summary: When tool_call_mcp_elicitation is set to false, Codex still sends elicitation.form during MCP initialize handshake, causing Graylog to reject the connection with error code -32603.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：MCP 集成是 Codex 与外部工具链（Graylog）对接的关键通道。feature flag `tool_call_mcp_elicitation=false` 本应禁用 elicitation.form 但未生效，导致 MCP initialize 握手失败（-32603），企业用户的基础设施集成完全不可用。明确的用户影响证据（Graylog 连接被拒绝）+ feature flag 行为不符合预期，属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: tool_call_mcp_elicitation=false does not suppress elicitation.form in MCP initialize (Graylog handshake fails with -32603)
source_issues.evidence: Setting tool_call_mcp_elicitation=false fails to suppress elicitation.form in MCP initialize, causing Graylog to reject the handshake with -32603. Entire MCP integration blocked.

signals.topic: CLI/TUI output truncation and visual glitches block session resume
signals.summary: Terminal output is truncated at end of turn with visual glitches (duplicated input GUI), and resume either crashes or shows 'Already viewing' without providing a resume ID. Users lose conversational context and cannot recover their session.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：CLI 是 Codex 的核心使用界面。输出截断导致用户丢失上下文信息，resume 功能崩溃或无法提供 resume ID，用户必须从头开始会话。对于长时间复杂任务，这意味着重新输入 context 的显著时间成本，属于关键体验下降。

source_issues.title: Truncated / corrupted CLI output with visual glitches and issues resuming
source_issues.evidence: Terminal truncated at end of turn with visual glitches (duplicated input GUI). Resume either crashes or shows 'Already viewing' without providing a resume ID. Session context is lost.

signals.topic: App resets to New chat view unexpectedly while idle on Windows
signals.summary: Codex desktop app on Windows switches to 'New chat' view on its own after being left idle, causing the user to lose their current thread context without any user action.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：用户正在进行的对话在空闲后被意外重置到空白聊天页，虽然线程在侧边栏中仍然存在，但主视图丢失。当前工作上下文中断，需重新定位并点击侧边栏恢复会话。对多任务用户造成明显的上下文丢失体验。

source_issues.title: Bug: app switches to New chat on its own while idle
source_issues.evidence: App jumps to a new empty chat without user interaction after being left idle. Current thread is lost from main view even though it remains in the sidebar. User loses context of active work.

signals.topic: Sanitizer strips required `id` field from built-in tool-call items, causing OpenAIConversationsSession to produce 400 API errors
signals.summary: In `session_persistence.py`, the `_sanitize_openai_conversation_item()` function unconditionally strips `id` from all conversation items. For built-in types `file_search_call`, `code_interpreter_call`, and `web_search_call`, the `id` field is required by the OpenAI Conversations API. When these sanitized items are passed to `add_items()`, the API returns `400 Missing required parameter: 'items[0].id'`, breaking the FileSearchTool workflow end-to-end.
aliases: sanitizer strips id from tool-call items
signals.review_reason: Confirmed API-level 400 error that breaks FileSearchTool when used with OpenAIConversationsSession. This is a main-flow failure — users cannot complete multi-turn conversations with file search tools. The bug is precisely located and reproducible.

source_issues.title: _sanitize_openai_conversation_item strips required id from built-in tool-call items
source_issues.evidence: The sanitizer removes `id` from all items, causing the OpenAI Conversations API to return 400 Missing required parameter. Reproduction involves FileSearchTool + OpenAIConversationsSession + multi-turn conversation, resulting in API rejection on turn 2.

signals.topic: Eager `sqlite3` import blocks deployment on minimal Python environments (Google Cloud Run)
signals.summary: The `agents` package eagerly imports `sqlite3` at module load time, causing immediate `ModuleNotFoundError` on Python images that ship without sqlite3 (e.g., Google Cloud Run slim base images). Users are blocked from deploying applications that import the agents package, even when they don't use sqlite3-dependent features.
aliases: sqlite3 not available in minimal images
signals.review_reason: Module-level import causes deployment startup crash on common minimal Python environments. This is a startup-time blocker — the app fails to even start on Google Cloud Run's slim image. User lost an hour of service due to this.

source_issues.title: Don't eagerly import sqlite3
source_issues.evidence: User deployed to Google Cloud Run and the app failed immediately because sqlite3 is not included in the default image. User had no sqlite3-dependent features enabled. Workaround required switching base image, costing an hour of downtime.

signals.topic: Tracing export RecursionError when truncating LLM responses containing `None` values
signals.summary: In `BackendSpanExporter`, `_truncate_json_value_for_limit()` returns `_truncated_preview(value)` (a dict) for non-str/dict/list values including `None`. This preview dict is then treated as a normal mapping by `_truncate_mapping_for_json_limit()`, causing recursive re-truncation of the preview structure itself and eventually a stack overflow (RecursionError). This crashes trace export and hides the original run error.
signals.review_reason: RecursionError causes trace export to crash and silently hides the original agent run error. This is a critical debugging failure — users cannot diagnose why their agent runs failed because the trace export itself crashes first. Root cause is well-identified in the truncation logic.

source_issues.title: RecursionError in tracing truncation: preview dict recursively re-truncated when message content is None
source_issues.evidence: When LLM response contains `None` values (common in assistant messages) and truncation is triggered, the trace export crashes with maximum recursion depth exceeded. The RecursionError in trace sanitization then masks the original run error, making debugging impossible.

signals.topic: GPT-5.1/GPT-5.4 `/v1/responses` endpoint silently hangs 10–28% of concurrent requests with no error response
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5+ simultaneous calls), 10–28% of requests to the `/v1/responses` endpoint hang indefinitely — TCP handshake completes but no HTTP response ever arrives, no timeout is triggered by the SDK, and the request blocks until caller-kill. Both raw `AsyncOpenAI` and Agents SDK `Runner.run()` are affected at the same rate, confirming the issue is in the OpenAI endpoint. This causes applications to hang and is a severe reliability failure for production deployments.
signals.review_reason: 10-28% of concurrent requests hang silently with no error, no timeout, and no retry — a catastrophic reliability failure for any production concurrent workload. Although the issue is technically in the OpenAI API endpoint, it directly manifests in and blocks Agents SDK users' main workflows. Users are left with no diagnostic signal because no HTTP error is ever returned.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: Multi-hour testing across 4 runs (200 total calls) showed 10-28% silent hangs. Requests accept TCP connection but receive no HTTP response. The SDK cannot retry because no error is received. Both raw OpenAI client and Agents SDK hang at identical rates, confirming API-level failure. Latencies of hung requests range 32-49s before caller timeout.

signals.topic: Computer interface silently drops modifier keys (`keys` parameter) from API response, breaking Shift+click, Ctrl+click, etc.
signals.summary: The OpenAI API's computer tool actions support an optional `keys` parameter for holding modifier keys while clicking (e.g., Shift+click, Ctrl+click, Alt+drag). The SDK's Computer and AsyncComputer abstract classes do not expose this parameter, and the action dispatch in `tool_actions.py` silently drops `action.keys` from the model response. All 5 action types (click, double_click, drag, move, scroll) are affected.
aliases: modifier keys not passed to Computer actions
keys parameter dropped from click/drag actions
signals.review_reason: Standard desktop operations (Shift+click, Ctrl+click, Alt+drag) silently fail because `keys` is dropped from all computer tool actions. This is not a minor edge case — modifier-key operations are fundamental to computer use. The silent data loss (no error, no warning) makes the failure invisible to users.

source_issues.title: Computer interface silently drops modifier keys (keys param) from API response
source_issues.evidence: API types (`ActionClick.keys`, `ActionDoubleClick.keys`, etc.) are part of the GA computer tool. The SDK silently drops them with no warning or error. Standard desktop operations (Shift+click for multi-select, Ctrl+click for new tab) silently fail. Silent data loss — no exception, no log.

signals.topic: Batch API returns 404 for GPT-5.x models due to automatic -batch suffix appended by backend
signals.summary: When using /v1/chat/completions endpoint with GPT-5.x models in Batch API, OpenAI's backend appends `-batch` to the model name internally, but the batch model variant does not exist, resulting in 404 model_not_found errors. The same models work fine with /v1/responses or GPT-4o models in Batch API.
aliases: batch api gpt-5 model not found
signals.review_reason: Batch job workflow is completely blocked for GPT-5.x users via /v1/chat/completions. The batch completes but every request returns 404 with model_not_found, wasting the batch job execution cost with zero output. While count=1, the user impact is severe (complete workflow failure + cost waste) and the underlying bug is specific to GPT-5 model family with Batch API.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Batch API returns 404 with GPT-5.x models
source_issues.evidence: Batch API with GPT-5.x via /v1/chat/completions fails with 404 model_not_found because backend appends '-batch' suffix internally but the variant does not exist. GPT-4o works fine with same code. GPT-5 via /v1/responses also works. Complete workflow failure for GPT-5 batch jobs.

signals.topic: Server-side compaction events not emitted during consecutive function_call-only turns in Responses API
signals.summary: When using context_management compaction in Responses API, compaction events are not emitted in output when the model returns only function_call items. Compaction only appears once an assistant message is finally returned. This causes context to grow unbounded in tool-heavy agent loops, eventually leading to context_length_exceeded errors.
aliases: compaction not emitted on function_call turns
context grows without compaction in tool loops
Responses API compaction missing on tool calls
signals.review_reason: Agent loops with multiple tool calls are a core use case for the Responses API. The compaction mechanism fails silently during function_call-only turns, causing context accumulation that can lead to context_length_exceeded — a blocking failure for long-running agent workflows. Clear user impact demonstrated with reproducible token count growth evidence.

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: In agent loops with consecutive function_call-only turns, context_tokens keep growing (5084 -> 5119 -> 5154) without any compaction event being emitted. Compaction only appears once model returns a message. Users hit context_length_exceeded before compaction starts working in tool-heavy workflows.

signals.topic: All requests blocked with OpenAIException 'Your request was blocked' when using custom API base URL
signals.summary: Any API request sent through the SDK with a custom base_url immediately returns OpenAIException with message 'Your request was blocked', even though the same request works with direct HTTP requests or other libraries. This completely breaks the SDK for Azure OpenAI, custom endpoints, and proxy setups.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow blocker for all users with custom API base URLs (Azure OpenAI, proxies, enterprise endpoints). The SDK is unusable for these common deployment patterns while the underlying API works fine with direct HTTP. The issue has been open since Feb 2026 with 4 comments indicating it remains unresolved.

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – 'Your request was blocked' with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: Every request with a custom base_url returns 'Your request was blocked'. Same request works fine with direct HTTP requests, proving the API and credentials are valid. Issue affects all custom base URL use cases including Azure OpenAI and proxies.

signals.topic: Persistent sessions resume fails: sessionDir field is null, causing 'prompt' to report 'No acpx session found'
signals.summary: When creating persistent sessions, the session index JSON correctly registers the session (visible via `status` and `sessions` commands), but the `sessionDir` field is written as `null`. When the user later tries to run `prompt` to resume the session, the code attempts to resolve the actual session directory from `sessionDir`, which is null, causing the prompt command to fail with 'No acpx session found'. The session exists in the index but is unresumable — a complete block on the persistent session workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow block for persistent sessions. The session is created and registered (visible in `status`/`sessions`), but `prompt` — the core resume action — is completely broken because sessionDir is null. This is not a cosmetic issue; it makes the persistent session feature non-functional for affected users. Count=1 is accurate per file.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt cannot find session
source_issues.evidence: Steps to reproduce provided: session is created and visible via `status` and `sessions`, but `prompt` fails with 'No acpx session found' because sessionDir is null in the index JSON. Root cause identified: sessionDir field written as null at session creation time.

signals.topic: WSL to Windows agent spawning fails due to untranslated Linux cwd paths sent to Windows .exe agents
signals.summary: When OpenClaw gateway runs on WSL2 and spawns a Windows agent binary (e.g., copilot.exe --acp), the cwd passed to `session/new` remains a Linux POSIX path (e.g., /home/user/.openclaw/workspace). Windows agents cannot resolve Linux filesystem paths and reject the session/new request with an error. Users on WSL who configure Windows .exe agents cannot initiate ACP sessions at all.
aliases: WSL path to Windows exe agent failure
signals.review_reason: This blocks the agent spawning workflow entirely for WSL users who rely on Windows agent binaries. The session/new request fails before any meaningful work can happen, making Windows agents unusable from WSL. Root cause and fix are clearly identified. Count=1 is accurate per file.

source_issues.title: WSL→Windows cwd path translation when spawning Windows .exe agents from WSL
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction with exact command configuration and error response provided. Root cause identified: asAbsoluteCwd() uses path.resolve which always produces POSIX paths on Linux/WSL, sent directly to Windows agent. Tested path formats table shows the issue clearly. Related issue openclaw/openclaw#42557 references same class of bug.

signals.topic: 安全扫描器将大量合法技能错误标记为 'Suspicious'，阻碍发布与发现
signals.summary: ClawHub 安全扫描器产生大量误报，将正常技能标记为可疑，导致合法技能无法正常展示、被用户信任使用或上架市场。
signals.review_reason: 13 条独立 issue 均来自不同技能作者，反映 ClawHub 安全扫描系统存在系统性误判问题。具体根因包括：(1) 扫描器读取注册表摘要时缺失 env/credential/homepage 字段导致所有声明凭证的技能被误标（issue #1618 明确指出影响 venice-api-kit、firecrawl-search 等多个技能）；(2) 本地文件 I/O、网络发送等合法行为模式被静态规则误判为可疑（issue #1616、#1615）；(3) VirusTotal 响应解析字段错误（issue #1612）。多条 issue 明确提到 VirusTotal 和 OpenClaw 双扫描仪均判定为 Benign 但仍被标记，说明误标非偶然。高频（count=13）、影响明确（合法技能无法正常展示、被市场标记为可疑），用户发布成本损失严重。
